mcqs.q: Article 262 of the Constitution deals with adjudication of disputes relating to waters of inter‑state rivers or river valleys. Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Article 262(1) empowers the Supreme Court to adjudicate such disputes.
options.B: Article 262(2) permits Parliament to exclude the jurisdiction of all courts, including the Supreme Court, in respect of such disputes.
options.C: Parliament has completely excluded the Supreme Court's jurisdiction under Article 136 in inter‑state water disputes.
options.D: Article 262 creates a permanent Inter‑State Water Disputes Tribunal.

mcqs.q: Consider the following statements about the Inter‑State Water Disputes Act, 1956: 1. It was enacted under Article 262(2) of the Constitution. 2. It provides for the constitution of a separate tribunal for each dispute. 3. The decisions of the tribunals are final and binding, but the Supreme Court can hear appeals under Article 136. Which of the above is/are correct?

The 2002 amendment to the Inter‑State Water Disputes Act brought which of the following changes? 1. A time limit of 3 years for the tribunal to give its award, extendable by 2 years. 2. Establishment of a Data Bank and Information System. 3. Replacement of all existing tribunals with a single permanent tribunal.
The award of an Inter‑State Water Disputes Tribunal, once published in the Official Gazette, has the force of a decree of the Supreme Court. This means:

options.A: The award cannot be questioned before any court.
options.B: The Supreme Court can entertain appeals under Article 136 in special circumstances.
options.C: The award is automatically executed without any further action.
options.D: Both A and B are correct as per judicial interpretation.

options.B: It cannot entertain any challenge to the tribunal's award under any circumstances.
options.C: Only the President can modify the award.
options.D: The Parliament can overrule the award.
